column1:
- Macro tone from the FOMC statement is positive: strong growth, low unemployment, inflation near 2%, and balanced risks; policy remains accommodative with gradual hikes expected.
- Beige Book corroborates broad strength: districts report growth (e.g., St. Louis), solid consumer spending (Dallas and Richmond), with Dallas buoyed by the energy sector.
- Labor markets are tight across occupations (engineers, manufacturing workers, IT professionals, truck drivers). Firms are raising compensation/benefits, converting workers to permanent roles, and leaning on longer hours to attract and retain employees—signs of mounting wage pressures.
- Pricing: most districts report higher prices and expect pricing pressures to intensify; final selling prices are rising, pointing to firmer inflation pressures than a macro-only read might imply.
- Headwinds: interest rates are weighing on existing home sales; agricultural commodity prices are mixed. April SLOOS points to slightly tighter financial conditions at the margin (wider loan spreads, some CRE policy changes) even as banks keep extending credit and jumbo standards remain unchanged.
- Net: still solid and accommodative backdrop, but somewhat less upbeat due to tighter labor supply, firmer price pressures, and rate-sensitive sector softness.
